title: Training Plan Import
description: A training plan importable by AccelerometerLifting. LLMs generating plans MUST conform to this schema exactly.

schemaVersion.description: Which version of this contract a document declares. 1.6 added the optional exercise key `prep_s`; what it means is stated once, at $defs.exercise.prep_s. Purely additive -- no key from 1.5 changed type, meaning or acceptance, so every 1.5 document is a valid 1.6 document. It is a new version rather than an extension of 1.5 because 1.5 shipped in v0.1.41 meaning the contract with implementCount and without prep_s. A build predating 1.6 refuses a document declaring 1.6, names the version and stages nothing; a build that supports 1.5 but not 1.6 -- v0.1.41, the only released one -- handed prep_s under 1.5 stages the plan, reports success and runs its own fixed 5 s prep, an unrecognised key being a warning rather than an error. The refusal is legible, the substituted prep is not. 1.7: prep_s also applies to a TIMED set -- a hold or a carry. No key is added, removed or retyped, and every 1.6 document is a valid 1.7 document; what changes is what the app does with a prep_s declared on a hold. Under 1.6 it is inert and the import gate says so; under 1.7 the prep plays and the set's clock does not start until it ends, so the prep is never counted into the duration the set records. It is a new version rather than an edit to 1.6 because 1.6 shipped in v0.1.42 meaning prep_s applies ONLY to sets carrying a tempo -- read at the tag -- and redefining a released version is not a resolution available here. A build predating 1.7 refuses a document declaring 1.7, names the version and stages nothing. The same document declared as 1.6 is accepted by that build, which warns on every hold that the declaration has no effect and then runs the hold with no prep. That warning is legible, unlike the substituted prep 1.6 was introduced to prevent; 1.7 is therefore about naming which contract a document was written against, not about preventing a silent loss. 1.8: adds the optional exercise keys `description` and `additional_notes`, splitting what used to be one `notes` blob into the part the lifter reads between sets without touching the phone and the part one tap reveals. `description` is capped at 220 characters, the only length limit anywhere in this contract; `additional_notes` has none, because it is where the overflow goes. Purely additive -- `notes` is unchanged in type, acceptance and meaning at every level it appears, so every 1.7 document is a valid 1.8 document and loses no text: with no `description`, an exercise's `notes` is still what takes the visible line without a tap. It is not drawn identically. A cue longer than the four-line collapsed cap is now cut with an ellipsis and a labelled SHOW MORE control, and the remainder is one tap away rather than on the screen. Declaring `description` AND `notes` on one exercise is legal and drops neither -- the description shows, the notes move behind the tap, and the import gate says which is which. A build predating 1.8 refuses a document declaring 1.8, names the version and stages nothing. The same document declared as 1.7 is accepted by that build, which reports `description` and `additional_notes` as unknown keys it ignored -- so the cue the author front-loaded is not shown at all, and only the ignored-key line at the gate says so. That is legible but lossy, which is what the version is for: it names which of the two shapes a document's coaching text is in. 1.8 is UNRELEASED until v0.1.44 ships, so further keys added in this release window extend 1.8 rather than minting 1.9 -- the sensors declaration of issue #156 and the bodyweight declaration of issue #161 both land under 1.8 if they land before that tag. THE FIRST OF THOSE HAS LANDED: 1.8 also adds the optional key `sensors`, on an exercise and on a set, declaring how many accelerometers the set is recorded with -- 1 (the default) or 2. Purely additive on the same terms as the coaching-text split: no key from 1.7 changes type, meaning or acceptance, every 1.7 document is a valid 1.8 document, and an omitted `sensors` is one sensor, which is what every plan written so far already means. It extends 1.8 rather than minting 1.9 because 1.8 has not shipped in any release, so there is no build in the world holding a definition of 1.8 without this key and no version boundary is being rewritten. A build predating 1.8 refuses the document by version, as before. The same document declared as 1.7 is accepted by such a build, which lists `sensors` among the keys it ignored and then records every set with one sensor -- legible at the gate, and lossy only in that the second stream is never captured. THE SECOND OF THOSE TWO HAS NOW LANDED TOO: 1.8 also adds the optional TOP-LEVEL keys `bodyweight_kg` and `bodyweight_lb` (issue #161), at most one of them, carrying the lifter's own body weight so the app can stop asking for a figure the coach already knows. Purely additive on the same terms again: no key from 1.7 changes type, meaning or acceptance, and every 1.7 document is a valid 1.8 document. It extends 1.8 for the same reason the sensors declaration did -- 1.8 has shipped in no release, so no build in the world holds a definition of 1.8 without these keys. Both are NULLABLE, and a null and an omission mean the same thing: nothing is written and whatever body weight the app already holds stands. Only a present, non-null, positive value is applied, and it is applied on import, overwriting whatever was stored -- there is no hierarchy between a plan and the app's own dialog, only recency. A build predating 1.8 refuses the document by version, as before; the same document declared as 1.7 is accepted by such a build, which lists the bodyweight among the keys it ignored and goes on using the figure it already had, which is legible at the gate and loses nothing. Versions 1.0 through 1.5 are not described here -- this record starts at 1.6 rather than backfilling six entries from memory. 1.9: adds the optional SET key `warmup`, declaring that a set is preparatory -- a ramp set, a warm-up, work that is not the training stimulus. Purely additive: no key from 1.8 changes type, meaning or acceptance, an omitted `warmup` is a working set, and every 1.8 document is a valid 1.9 document. It is a new version rather than an extension of 1.8 because 1.8 SHIPPED in v0.1.44 -- read at the tag, not assumed -- so the window in which the sensors and bodyweight keys could extend it is closed. What the key is FOR is the half a plan author must not miss: until now warm-up was not a plan declaration at all but an effort TILE in the app, and tapping it stored `warmup: true` together with `rpe: null`, so the effort of every warm-up set was discarded by construction. A 500 lb squatter's empty-bar ramp set is a warm-up by PURPOSE, and what it felt like is a separate, knowable fact worth keeping. From v0.1.45 the tile is gone, this key is the only producer of `warmup`, and warm-up sets carry a real effort rating like any other set -- which is also why the published export description of `warmup` no longer tells a reader to exclude those sets from effort analysis. A build predating 1.9 refuses a document declaring 1.9, names the version and stages nothing. The same document declared as 1.8 is accepted by such a build, which lists `warmup` among the keys it ignored and then records every set as working -- legible at the gate, and lossy only in that the ramp sets are indistinguishable from work in that session's export. 1.10: the exercise key `sensors` and its per-set override stop deciding anything. They are still ACCEPTED and still validated to 1 or 2, so every 1.9 document imports unchanged and nothing is refused; they are ignored, and the import gate says so on any plan that declares one. What replaces them is the hardware: the app records from whatever accelerometers are CONNECTED -- one bar sensor writes one stream, two connected units labelled A and B write two -- on every set of every exercise. The owner's rule: "If you've got one use one, if you've got two, use both." NOT additive: no key is added, removed or retyped, but a key's MEANING changed, which is the kind of change a reader has to be told about rather than discover. It is a new version rather than an edit to 1.9 because 1.9 SHIPPED in v0.1.45 -- read at the tag, not assumed -- and redefining a released version is not a resolution available here. A build predating 1.10 refuses a document declaring 1.10, names the version and stages nothing. The same document declared as 1.9 is accepted by such a build, which then HONOURS the count and records one stream where this build would record two; that is legible only in that build's own export, which says what it armed. Labelling both units A and B in the app is still required and is not a count: two 20-byte WitMotion frames carry no checksum, so two streams the app cannot tell apart interleave into plausible samples rather than into an error. 1.11: adds the optional EXERCISE key `progression`, naming which dimension of that exercise moves when the lifter rates a set as having had more in it -- "weight", "reps", "time" or "none". The app's post-set effort scale already asks how much more a set had in it; from 1.11 a set rated on the headroom end, that is not a warm-up and that has sets left on its exercise, offers a small grid to put that answer onto the NEXT set, and this key says what the grid raises: load (5-30 lb, or an authored 2.5-15 kg row), reps (+1/+2), the hold (+5/+10/+15 s), or nothing at all. Purely additive. No key from 1.10 is added to, removed or retyped, and OMITTING IT MEANS "weight", so every 1.10 document is a valid 1.11 document and behaves identically to the way it behaved before this key existed. "none" is NOT the same as omitting it: omitting it is a plan with no opinion, on which load moves; "none" is a plan whose opinion is that this exercise holds its load and its reps across its sets, and the grid is not shown for it however the set was rated. It is a new version rather than an extension of 1.10 because 1.10 SHIPPED in v0.1.48 -- read at the tag, not assumed -- and redefining a released version is not a resolution available here. A build predating 1.11 refuses a document declaring 1.11, names the version and stages nothing. The same document declared as 1.10 is accepted by such a build, which lists `progression` among the keys it ignored and then offers the load grid on every exercise -- legible at the gate, and lossy only in that an exercise the author meant to hold, or to step on reps, is offered load instead. A "reps" declared on an exercise whose sets are all timed, or a "time" on one whose sets are all prescribed in reps, is accepted and warned about once per exercise: there is nothing of that kind to raise, so the grid would draw empty. The key decides only what the grid OFFERS -- the lifter can still change load, reps, hold and tempo from the app's own change-next-set dialog on any exercise, whatever it says. 1.12: the exercise keys `sensorOnStack`, `bodyweight` and `sensorInverted` are declared NULLABLE, and one rule governs all three, stated here once rather than three times over the properties: an absent key and a null are the same thing and neither is a declaration. It says the plan has no opinion, and the app's own definition of that exercise stands. A key written true or false IS a declaration and beats that definition either way, which is the point of being able to write false. Which ids carry a built-in default under this rule is stated at each property: `sensorOnStack` on the stack machines it lists, `bodyweight` on the ids named at $defs.exercise.bodyweight, and `sensorInverted` on NONE -- no exercise the app ships is inverted by construction, because inversion is a property of how a machine is routed rather than of which machine it is, so an omitted `sensorInverted` resolves to false exactly as it did at 1.11. The import gate names each inference it makes, one line per exercise whose key it had to decide: a stack default and a body-weight default each get one, and `sensorInverted` gets none because there is nothing to infer. Every 1.11 document is a valid 1.12 document and imports to exactly the same geometry -- no key is added, removed or renamed, and nothing that validated before is refused. What widens is the accepted TYPE of three existing keys, which now admit null; a plan that spelled absence as null was refused by this document at 1.11 and accepted by the app, and that disagreement is half of what this version is for. The other half is that the app has read an omitted `sensorOnStack` as undeclared since v0.1.49, and an omitted `bodyweight` as undeclared since #227, which shipped in v0.1.50, while this document still typed both as plain booleans, so the published contract and the shipped app disagreed about what an absent key meant; `sensorInverted` is given the same shape at the same time. It is a new version rather than an edit to 1.11 because 1.11 SHIPPED in v0.1.49 -- read at the tag, not assumed -- and redefining a released version is not a resolution available here. A build predating 1.12 refuses a document declaring 1.12, names the version and stages nothing. The same document declared as 1.11 is accepted by such a build and behaves identically, with one exception: a null written against any of the three is refused by the 1.11 schema, so a plan that spells absence that way should declare 1.12 or omit the key instead.

bodyweight_kg.description: The lifter's body weight in kilograms, used purely for load arithmetic: on every exercise declaring "bodyweight": true the plan states only what is ADDED or what assists the lifter, so the total load is body weight plus that. It is not a health datum. DECLARED ON THE PLAN, not on a session: a plan is authored in one sitting at one body weight, and the app stores exactly one figure, so a per-session key would raise a question about which session's value wins that has no honest answer. At most one of bodyweight_kg / bodyweight_lb. Writing null for BOTH keys, or a null beside a figure in the other unit, is the same as omitting the null one and is valid; only two non-null figures are refused. Use a real measurement of this lifter from any source genuinely available -- a connected scale, a health platform, a conversation with the lifter, or a session export -- rather than only a figure the lifter typed directly. A measurement up to FOURTEEN DAYS old is fit for purpose, matching the app's own threshold before it asks the lifter again, so this contract and the app never disagree about what counts as current. OMIT THIS KEY OR WRITE null for anything older than that, or if the weight is not known at all -- the two mean exactly the same thing, neither writes anything, and whatever the lifter last entered in the app stands; the app stamps a written value with the moment the plan is imported, so supplying a stale reading as current would make that stamp wrong. NEVER GUESS IT -- not from the lifter's lifts, not from a typical lifter, not from an old plan. This figure becomes the base load of every set of every exercise declaring "bodyweight": true, so a guessed value silently mis-states the recorded load and the power of all bodyweight work, passes every validation, warns about nothing, and cannot be recovered from the recording afterwards. A present, non-null, positive value is applied on import: it overwrites whatever body weight the app was holding, and the app's own dialog overwrites it back the next time the lifter uses it. Neither source is privileged; the most recent write is the one that stands. The import gate names the number that was applied, so the change is visible rather than discovered later.

bodyweight_lb.description: The lifter's body weight in pounds, converted to kilograms on import. What it means, when to omit it, and why a guess is worse than an omission are stated once, at properties.bodyweight_kg.

exercise.description: Exercise id, snake_case (e.g. back_squat). Unknown ids create a custom exercise on import.

notes.description: The whole coach comment (form cues, intent) as a single string. Still accepted and still shown with each set of this exercise when no `description` is declared, so no plan written before 1.8 loses any of it. It is not drawn identically: past the four-line collapsed cap it is cut with an ellipsis and a labelled SHOW MORE control, and the rest is one tap away. A plan written NOW should use `description` for the part the lifter must read between sets and `additional_notes` for the rest, because that decides which half is visible without a tap. Declaring `notes` alongside `description` is legal and loses nothing: the description shows and the notes move behind the expand tap, and the import gate says so.

description.description: The part of the coaching cue the lifter reads between sets WITHOUT touching the phone: the thing that decides how the next set is performed. Hard limit 220 characters, which is roughly four lines on a phone at the default font scale; a document over it is refused at the import gate, naming the path, rather than being cut off mid-sentence. Put the cue that matters FIRST and put everything else in `additional_notes` -- a safety cue written second is a safety cue behind a tap.

additional_notes.description: Everything the cue says beyond `description` -- the paragraph, the setup ritual, the background. Shown only when the lifter expands the note, so nothing that decides how the set is performed belongs here. No length limit: this is where the overflow from `description` goes.

start.description: Where the lift BEGINS, so the app knows which way the first movement of every rep goes. 'top' = starts at the top, first movement is down (squat, bench, leg curl). 'bottom' = starts at the bottom, first movement is up (press from the rack, deadlift, leg press). 'down'/'up' name that first movement directly and are equivalent. Machines of the same movement pattern genuinely differ, so declare it. Omitted: inferred from the exercise id, which is a guess.

concentric.description: Which way the CONCENTRIC (driving) phase moves. Default 'up'. Use 'down' for leg curls, lat pulldowns and pushdowns. Independent of 'start': that says which phase comes first, this says which direction the drive goes, and together they decide which tempo digit is the eccentric.

sensorInverted.description: True when the sensor moves OPPOSITE to the load the lifter drives — common on a cable machine, where the sensor rides the weight stack, so pulling the handle down sends the stack (and the sensor) up. Without this, every phase label and velocity on that exercise is backwards. No exercise the app ships is inverted by construction, so there is no built-in default behind an omitted key here and one resolves to false -- the key is nullable so that a plan can say false as a decision rather than by silence. From 1.12 this key may also be written null; what an absent or null value means is stated once, in the 1.12 entry of the version log above.

travelRatio.description: Lifter-side travel per unit of sensor travel, for pulleys that are not 1:1. A 2:1 cable moves the handle twice as far as the stack, so 2. Default 1.

prep_s.description: Seconds of prep before each set of this exercise: the pause between my starting the set and the set actually beginning. Estimate THE TIME MY HANDS ARE UNAVAILABLE -- fastening straps, chalking, setting a hook grip, cinching a belt, lying down on a machine -- not the walk to the rack or loading plates, which happen before I start the set. A Romanian deadlift with straps is not ready five seconds after I tap START; a cable machine is ready in two. APPLIES TO A SET CARRYING A tempo, where the prep runs into the first movement call, AND TO A TIMED SET OF a hold or a carry, where it runs into the word that starts the clock -- on those the clock does not start until the prep ends, so the prep is never counted into the duration the set records. Declared anywhere else it does nothing, and the app says so at the import gate. Omitted means 5. I can change it in the app, and the change comes back in the session export as prep_s beside plannedPrep_s -- author the next plan from that rather than guessing again.

sensors.description: ACCEPTED BUT IGNORED since 1.10. It used to say how many accelerometers each set of this exercise is recorded with; it decides nothing now. The app records from whatever accelerometers are CONNECTED: one bar sensor writes one stream, two connected units that I have labelled A and B in the app write two, on every set of every exercise. Leave it out of new plans -- it stays accepted only so a plan written against 1.8 or 1.9 still imports, and the import gate lists it as having no effect. Still validated to 1 or 2, so a 3 is still refused with the path named. The labels A and B are the identity of the physical units and say NOTHING about which end of the bar or which hand each was on -- that is assigned in analysis afterwards, so a swapped mounting costs nothing. Labelling is required even though counting is not: two 20-byte WitMotion frames carry no checksum, so two streams the app cannot tell apart interleave into plausible samples rather than into an error.

optional.description: Accessory work that may be dropped when the session runs long. Surfaced in the app so the decision is planned rather than improvised.

progression.description: Which dimension of this exercise goes UP when I rate a set as having had more in it. After every set I tap how it felt; a rating on the headroom end of that scale means I could have done more, and if the set was not a warm-up and the exercise has sets left, the app offers a small grid to put that onto the next set. This key says what the grid raises. "weight" offers 5-30 lb (or an authored 2.5-15 kg row) -- use it for anything with a load ladder. "reps" offers +1 and +2 reps -- use it where the load is fixed and the progression is volume, such as bodyweight work with no way to add plates. "time" offers +5, +10 and +15 seconds -- use it on holds and carries. "none" shows NO grid at all: use it where the point is to hold load and reps across the exercise's sets, and I should not be prompted upward however a set felt. OMITTED MEANS "weight", so leaving it out is the same as writing "weight" and no plan written before 1.11 changes behaviour. Omitting it and writing "none" are NOT the same thing. Declare "reps" only on an exercise with rep-prescribed sets and "time" only on one with timed sets; the other way round the app accepts the plan and says at the import gate that the grid has nothing to offer. This decides only what is OFFERED -- I can still change load, reps, hold and tempo myself on any exercise from the app's change-next-set screen.

plane.description: The plane the LIFTER moves in. 'horizontal' for seated rows, chest-press machines and horizontal cable work. This also changes how the tempo digits are read: vertical work reads them positionally (digit 1 = down stroke), while horizontal work has no up or down and reads them by phase (digit 1 = eccentric, digit 3 = concentric). Note this is the lifter's plane, not the sensor's — see sensorOnStack.

sensorOnStack.description: True when the sensor rides a cable weight stack. The stack travels VERTICALLY however the lifter moves, so a seated row measured off the stack is a vertical measurement of a horizontal exercise — set this together with plane: 'horizontal' and sensorInverted as the routing requires. On the machines the app ships a mount for -- the assisted pull-up, chin-up and dip machines, the lat pulldown, seated row, seated cable row, cable row and triceps pushdown, the leg curl, seated and lying leg curl and leg extension -- an omitted key resolves to the stack, and the import gate says so. Declare false to say the sensor was on the handle. This adds no key and did not move the plan format, which read 1.10 when that seeding landed; 1.11 was minted afterwards for a different key, `progression`. From 1.12 this key may also be written null; what an absent or null value means is stated once, in the 1.12 entry of the version log above.

bodyweight.description: True when the lifter's own body is the load — pull-ups, dips, push-ups. The set's load_kg/load_lb is then what was ADDED, and may be NEGATIVE for band or machine assistance. Total load is the lifter's body weight (set in the app) plus that. On pull_up, chin_up, dip, push_up, dead_hang, muscle_up, inverted_row and rope_dead_hang -- ids the app ships as body-weight work by construction -- an omitted key resolves to true, and the import gate says so. Declare false if the load on one of those eight ids is not the lifter's own body. This adds no key and did not move the plan format, which read 1.11 when that seeding landed. From 1.12 this key may also be written null; what an absent or null value means is stated once, in the 1.12 entry of the version log above.

implementCount.description: How many IDENTICAL objects are held at once — 2 for a pair of dumbbells or a two-handled farmer's walk; 1 (the default) for a barbell, a machine, a goblet squat, a single-arm row, or one dumbbell held on a weighted dip. This does NOT change what load_kg / load_lb mean: those are ALWAYS the TOTAL across everything held. A pair of 40 lb dumbbells is "implementCount": 2 with "load_lb": 80, and the app shows it as 2 × 40 lb. Writing 40 there records half the weight lifted, and nothing afterwards can tell it apart from a real 40 lb set. It is NOT a count of limbs and must NEVER be taken from "side": a rear-foot-elevated split squat holding two dumbbells is "side": "left" WITH "implementCount": 2, and a suitcase carry is "side": "right" with "implementCount": 1. OMIT it when the objects are NOT identically loaded (40 lb in one hand, 30 in the other): give the true total and the app shows the total alone rather than inventing a split.

kind.description: How the movement is performed. 'dynamic' is ordinary rep work; 'hold' is an isometric; 'carry' is a loaded walk; 'explosive' is an Olympic-style lift judged on peak velocity with no tempo. This says what the movement IS, not how a set of it is measured — whether a set runs on reps or on the clock comes from the set's own reps / duration_s. Omitted: the app uses its built-in definition if the id is one it ships, otherwise guesses from the id, which matches word fragments and gets ordinary names wrong. Declaring it always wins, and any disagreement is flagged at the import gate.

reps.description: Rep count for dynamic sets. Provide exactly one of reps / duration_s.

duration_s.description: Hold/carry duration in seconds for timed sets (plank, farmer's walk). Provide exactly one of reps / duration_s.

load_kg.description: Load in kilograms. Provide at most one of load_kg / load_lb; omit both for bodyweight. May be negative on a bodyweight exercise (see bodyweight): a band or assist machine subtracts from body weight. Always the TOTAL across everything held, including when the exercise declares "implementCount": 2 — write 80 for a pair of 40 lb dumbbells, not 40.

load_lb.description: Load in pounds; converted to kg on import. Provide at most one of load_kg / load_lb; omit both for bodyweight. May be negative on a bodyweight exercise (see bodyweight): a band or assist machine subtracts from body weight. Always the TOTAL across everything held, including when the exercise declares "implementCount": 2 — write 80 for a pair of 40 lb dumbbells, not 40.

side.description: For unilateral exercises (side plank, suitcase carry, single-leg RDL): which side this set trains. Emit one set per side.

note.description: Commentary for THIS SET alone (the exercise-level 'notes' applies to all of its sets). E.g. 'closer to the plate, higher ROM'.

tempo.description: Four-digit tempo. The digits are POSITIONAL: digit 1 is the DOWN stroke, digit 2 the pause at the bottom, digit 3 the UP stroke, digit 4 the pause at the top. Which of the strokes is the eccentric follows from the exercise's 'concentric' direction, not from the digit order. 'X' in digit 3 means explosive. Dash form ('4-0-1-0') is accepted.

sensors.description: ACCEPTED BUT IGNORED since 1.10, exactly as $defs.exercise.sensors is, and for the reasons stated there. It used to override the exercise's declaration for one set; there is no declaration left to override.

warmup.description: True when this set is PREPARATORY -- a ramp set, a warm-up, work that is not the training stimulus. Declared here because warm-up-ness is what a set is FOR, which the plan's author knows and the app cannot infer; how the set FELT is a separate fact the lifter rates afterwards on the effort scale, and a warm-up now carries a real rating rather than none. Mark every preparatory set of a ramp individually: there is no exercise-level form of this key, because a block ramps and its warm-up singles and its working set are sets of the same exercise. Omitted means a working set, and there is no way to say "not known" -- an unmarked set is one the author considered work. It does not change how the set is recorded, cued or analysed; it is a label on the set's purpose that comes back in the session export as `warmup` UNLESS the lifter marks the set otherwise on the rest screen, in which case their mark wins and `warmupByLifter` says so -- see the session-export schema's own `warmup` description.
